title: Point to ai relay from --help and ai instructions
lead: `slicer ai relay` exists, but nothing points to it. `slicer --help` describes `ai` as "onboarding instructions for coding agents", and neither `ai instructions` nor `ai instructions --rest` names the relay. Name it in the top-level help and add a pointer to the guide part that `--rest` also prints.
findings_note: owner report, session 2026-10-09: slicer --help gives no sign of the relay; ai instructions and ai skill do not mention it (s241 left the pointer out of scope)
boundary: **Not in this slice:** changing the relay text, changing `skill_text` or the installed SKILL.md copies, and new `ai` subcommands.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: The owner looked at `slicer --help` and found no way to the relay. To find it, you have to guess that `ai` has subcommands and run `slicer ai --help`. Agents follow `ai instructions`, and agents that load the skill follow `ai instructions --rest`. Neither text mentions the relay, so an agent will not run a relay unless it is told the command name. s241 left the pointer out of scope on purpose. This slice adds it.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/cli.py`: the `help=` of the `ai` subparser (line 2722 at filing).
- `src/slicer/ai.py`: a one-line pointer in a part that both `INSTRUCTIONS` and `rest_text()` include (`IMPLEMENT_MORE` or `HANDOFF_SECTION`), so the skill text does not change.
- `docs/commands.md` and `README.md` if they quote the `ai` help line. `CHANGELOG.md`.
- `tests/test_ai.py`.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `test_TopLevelHelp_AiRow_NamesRelay`
2. `test_Instructions_PointToAiRelay`
3. `test_InstructionsRest_PointToAiRelay`
4. `test_SkillText_UnchangedByRelayPointer`: `skill_text()` contains no relay line, so the installed copies stay current.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Reword the `ai` help so it names the three subcommands, for example "agent onboarding: instructions, skill, relay". Add one sentence that tells an agent to run `slicer ai relay` to run one slice through implementer, reviewer, architect and gate agents. Put it in a part that both the full guide and `--rest` print. Keep it neutral about the finish step: it must not name `done`, so the handoff-project rule (a handoff guide never tells an agent to run `done`) still holds. Update any test that pins the guide or help text exactly.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: `python3 tests/affected.py --run`, then `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests`. `slicer --help` shows relay on the `ai` row. `slicer ai instructions` and `slicer ai instructions --rest` (plain and `--json`) both name `slicer ai relay`. `slicer ai skill` output is unchanged. `slicer check` passes. `git diff --check` is clean.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Branch `feature/s244-relay-pointer` in `.worktrees/s244`. Do not commit, merge, or push until the owner asks. This repo finishes with `handoff`.
